newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Gintian sees first-half profit.
newsitem.headline: Gintian sees first-half profit.

text.p: China's Gintian Industry (Group) Co Ltd said on Wednesday it expects to post a net profit of 50 million yuan for the first half of 1997 after reporting a substantial loss for 1996.

A company official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin the conglomerate would probably move out of the red for the whole of 1997, but declined to give a specific forecast for the whole year.
Gintian reported a net loss of 62.10 million yuan for 1996 based on international accounting standards, against a net profit of 10.22 million yuan in 1995, a company accountant said.
Gintian's expected profits for the first half of 1997 would be supported by the closure of unprofitable subsidiaries and the sale of completed residential properties, the company official said.
The company is involved in property development, textiles and foreign trade.
About 50 percent of its properties, mainly residential, are in Shenzhen, with the rest in other parts of China, he said.
Turnover reached 670.23 million yuan in 1996 compared with 901.19 million in 1995 based on Chinese standards, according to the company.
Gintian's B shares were trading around HK$3.56 in late afternoon, down HK$0.25 or 6.65 percent on volume of 531,700 shares, making it among the biggest losers amongst Shenzhen B shares on Wednesday.
The company proposed no dividend for 1996, pending approval of shareholders at a meeting on May 30.
